There were no obvious concerns noticed. Operator may proceed with installation of tacking on monument/vent marker. Please include a picture of installed monument/vent marker, prior to burial, and an as plugged wellbore schematic with the submission of the Certificate of Well Plugging for this well. There is an outstanding 78a81(a)2 violation on this well from 7/5/2019 that appears to have been addressed through plugging operations. There were no new violations noted during this inspection. This violation will be closed upon receipt of the plugging certificate.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Rockdale Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-03-16
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 880510
Permit API: 117-22060
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Union Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 2020-03-16
Comments: A routine inspection was conducted to assess overall conditions. A frac is on-going. I met with several Rockdale representatives during this inspection. Both of Rockdale's field technicians accompanied me on this inspection including Jen Compton. A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment to hold the produced water for the frac. Two aboveground storage tanks (AST) are also present and store freshwater. The tanks and their containment appear to be in good condition overall. Tarps are being used in the stormwater channels to prevent stormwater or other fluids from entering the northeast infiltration basin. Stormwater continues to pumped from the northeast basin and disposed of. Fluid is collecting in the northeast corner of the pad as it did in August 2019 while drilling was taking place on the pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of this fluid was approximately 2.3 mS/cm. Jen Compton said that she would have the fluid pumped out and that an investigation would be done to determined why the EC appears to be elevated. This is the same area where fluid with elevated conductivity collected while drilling was occurring on the pad. The Department recommends frequent monitoring of this area of the pad. The Department also recommends removing fluid that accumulates in this area of the pad as needed. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEP's Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.

In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/21/2023
Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
Violation ID: 8160131
Permit API: 015-23768
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/21/2023
Comments: I arrived to the location at 12:50pm. The weather was 68¿¿F and sunny at time of inspection. I met with Repsol representative Billy Watts on location for the inspection. Plugging work was being performed on this well (9H) at time of inspection. A gel plug was set in the hole with a top at 2,630'. The rig was planning to next run a Cement Bond Log (CBL) and continue with plugging operations. On 9/21/2023 (prior to my arrival onsite), the production casing was section milled and approximately 13’ of damaged casing was removed from the well. I visually inspected the section of removed casing during this inspection. The piece of casing that was on top of the 5 1/2" production casing string was a 3' pup joint. Approximately 1 1/2' down the 3' pup joint, 3 holes were noted in the casing. The dimensions of the holes ranged in size from approximately 1/8" to 2" and varied from a straight-lined crack to irregular and rounded in shape. While the damaged casing was visually observed during the inspection, Repsol did restrict my ability to document the condition of the removed section of casing by photograph. Although, Repsol provided photographs of the removed section of casing to the Department the next day (9/22/2023), this represents a violation of Section 3258(a) of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. ¿¿ 3258(a). I left the location at 1:45pm. In addition to citing this new violation, the outstanding violations that were previously cited (Inspection Record #3611541) were also noted as continuing during this inspection. Therefore, the Inspection Results Code used for this inspection report is Violation(s) and Recurring Violations (VRV). The PADEP requests that Respol include an explanation of the cause of this violation with the written response previously-requested in the NOV dated 8/28/2023 (Inspection Record #3611541).

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/14/2025
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8241005
Permit API: 015-23892
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/14/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) on 7/14/2025 at 0630 hours. The weather ranged from mid-70s to mid-80s degrees throughout the day. The inspection was conducted in response to a report of a well control incident occurring on the 7H well which resulted in a release of produced fluids. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #390569 is tied to the release in CTS.According to Repsol, at ~1830 hours on 7/13/2025 a pressure issue on the 7H well caused the uncontrolled release of produced fluid up the casing[s] to the pad surface. Efforts to control pressure and prevent the escaping fluids have failed so far. Secondary containments were overtopped and fluid has and continues to escape the pad surface. A temporary berm was constructed along the northwestern edge around the western corner of the pad, below the fill slope, to collect fluids (photos #3 to 5). The "corner" berm below the fill slope was said to be completed around 0000 hours on 7/14/2025. Numerous gravel berms were constructed on the pad surface to help prevent fluids from escaping the pad surface but are failing in numerous spots. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed sheet flowing from numerous areas along the southwestern edge of the pad (see photo #8 for example). Fluid observed in the western corner of the stormwater control basin was field measured for electrical conductivity and returned a reading of >19.99mS/cm. ~1000 hours: A Repsol representative onsite indicated that larger pumps were en route to catch up on fluid collection that is being pooled on the western corner of the well pad (photo #9). According to Repsol, the pumps being brought in should be able to catch up on the fluid that is pooled on the surface.A secondary berm/trench was constructed below the first "corner" berm below the fill slope sometime throughout the day. A break in the first berm was dug to allow fluid collected to flow into the secondary berm. The secondary berm is flowing fluid into the stormwater control basin onsite (see photos #10-12).Fluid was able to reach the stormwater control basin shown in photo #7. The DEP collected a sample for standard analysis code 942 from the basin which was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (Sample #0983-510).A third (tertiary) berm/trench was later constructed below the secondary berm and was built into the stormwater control basin. The short side wall of the basin was removed to allow for excess fluid build-up in the basin to collect in the third berm. The secondary and tertiary berms are utilized to relieve hydrostatic pressure from the "corner" berm. Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an incident response inspection that was conducted on-site.Kris Bowser with AMS Energy contacted me on Thursday, July 14, 2022, to report a brine spill that had occurred on AMS's Barrett Pattison 5 Well Site. The spill had been discovered earlier the same day. A valve had been broken off of a fiberglass brine tank that was used on-site. Kris believed that the valve had likely been damaged by an ATV that had gotten too close to the tank. Fluid from the tank had recently been hauled out. Kris estimated that less than a barrel of brine had been spilled onto the ground near the tank.Kris met me on-site to view the spill. The damaged valve had been repaired. Most of the spilled brine appeared to have settled in a swale that ran next to the tank. The impacted area was clearly marked with dead vegetation. My soil conductivity probe was used to verify the extent of the impacted area. Elevated readings were not observed beyond the area marked by the dead vegetation. A plan for addressing the impacted soil was discussed with Kris. The soil should be excavated and hauled to a landfill. Kris indicated the AMS would provide the Department with a receipt of disposal from the landfill once the soil has been disposed of.

Comments: On 12/12/2022, I conducted a follow up inspection of the DR02 Pad and Impoundment ESX 1H well. Nucomer has hired a 3rd party contractor "Assist" to complete the secondary containment liner repair. TJ Pennino from EMKEY Gathering was on site representing Nucomer Energy. This is in response to violations in previous inspections(3459581). The violations are for tears and holes in the secondary containment liner in the tank battery. Two different methods were being utilized in the repair attempt. One is a hot air weld of liner material. The second was a PVC extruder gun as seen in photo #3. It should be noted the original containment liner is thickness of 20 mil. The patch material brought by Assist for the hot air welding is a 40 mil thickness. After several attempts to hot air weld the patch material to the existing liner, it was evident trying to weld the 40 mil patch material to the 20 mil existing material was not going to work. Several pieces of the 20 mil liner were cut from outside containment and cleaned as best as possible. Again the original liner material is too thin and was not supporting a good hot-air weld. The extruder was used on several smaller holes. It became obvious it is not suitable to be used on a material of this thickness. The temperature was set as low as the machine would allow and the material melted through the original liner (pictures #1 and #4).After several attempts trying several different methods, the decision was made by TJ to abandon the repair attempt. TJ was going to speak with ASSIST and plan another course of action and discuss options available.Additionally the violation for the 55 gallon drums being stored outside of secondary containment, can be closed. This violation has been resolved.

Comments: On 03/12/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well site following violations issued on 12/19/2023 (IR 3662363, Enforcement 423308). I was accompanied by PA DEP Compliance Specialist, George Traister. Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) were issued on 12/19/2023. The violations were issued as outstanding on 01/31/2024 (IR 3704581).The following was observed on 03/12/2024:Conductivity readings were taken within the water and gravel in the tank battery. The valve on Tank 1 looked to be leaking fluid. Crystallization was noted on the valve (Photo 1). The water within the battery around Tank 1 did not display elevated readings (Photo 2). The fluid escaping from the valve is recommended to be addressed. A reading was obtained within the gravel around the pan of Tank 4. This reading was 4.28 mS (Photo 3).Readings were taken within the gravel in the battery around Tank 5 and within the fluid in the pan. The readings within the gravel were 4.76 mS and 4.26 mS (Photos 4, 5). The reading within the pan was 17.30 mS (Photos 6, 7), which may indicate fluids leaking from tank fluid removal or from the valve itself. I recommend that this is addressed. The piping on the drain from the battery has been shortened. The exterior end is capped, and no elevated conductivity was noted on the ground below. The interior end is open, and I recommend that this is also capped. The water level in the battery is close to the edge of the pipe (Photos 8, 9). Stabilization has been added to the earthen berm. I recommend that additional is added as needed (Photos 10, 11).Pans are under each tank valve (Photo 12).Wet spots were noted on the exterior of the earthen berm. Conductivity readings were taken within these noted areas and resulted in the following: 4.00 mS, 6.33 mS, 5.44 mS. Another reading resulted in 1.15 mS. I recommend that fluid from inside the battery is not migrate through the berm. Livestock activity in the vicinity is taken into consideration (Photos 13-17). The violations issued on 12/29/2023 and 01/31/2024 remain outstanding.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Broadleaf Holdings" Marcellus well site. Tory Rogers called the DEP on Friday morning May 23, 2025 to report a release of approximately 9 gallons of diesel based drilling mud released from a flare stack to the pad surface that morning. I met with Tory Rogers, Jim Brown, Megan DePue (all 3 Repsol), and Scotty Brown (DEP, OGI) on site. While drilling a future Marcellus Shale well there was a control issue, so they lit the flare stack to burn off natural gas incurred. Some drilling mud blew out of the flare stack, estimated at 7 gallons onto pad containment, and 9 gallons on the pad surface. Rogers showed us where the flare stack released drilling mud. Resource Environmental directed excavation to remove pad material the drilling mud impacted, which was approximately a 10'X60' area. They completed the cleanup around 1600 hrs the same day the release occurred. The material is in 2 dumpsters on the NE corner of the pad. I got a 1.5 ppm reading with a 10.6 eV MiniRae photoionization detector (PID) from the removed pad material, and a 0.0 ppm PID reading from the remediated pad surface, which indicates the cleanup sufficiently removed the impacted pad material. Drill cuttings in a dumpster near the drill rig gave a 135.7 ppm reading. Violations cited to the 015-23893 drilling permit are considered immediately corrected.Rogers explained they increased the density of the drill mud from 12.8 lbs/gal to 13.5 lbs/gal to provide more well control.Repsol laid the containment on this pad on February 26 thru March 3, 2025. Felt liner (130 mil thickness) went down first, then wood/steel mats. Fine gravel is used to fill gaps between the mats.Precision Drilling 110 started drilling 4 new Marcellus wells at this site on April 1 2025, and expect to finish drilling around June 10, 2025. There are also 4 existing Marcellus wells here. They drill on water based mud for the vertical section, then switch to diesel based mud for the kickoff (curve) and horizontal section.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity (EC) of 0.68-1.7 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.62FJLP

Comments: On 5/8/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 50 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Upon my arrival, I first inspected the original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well. A plugged well monument is installed above the well with a plugged date of 3/24/2025. All servicing equipment has been removed from this pad. I was unaccompanied when inspecting the north pad. There are five newly drilled and completed wells on site that were staged for production. Two sand separators were attached to each wellhead, the sand separators all connected to one gas-buster style frac tank. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs have been installed on site, all staged in secondary containment. Secondary containment remains installed around the wellheads. Patterson drilling rig #805 has been mobilized to the site to drill an additional eight wells at the site. The rig was towered up on the first well, the 206HU, and had started drilling on 4/30/2025. Secondary containment has been installed for drilling operations. Nine frac tanks, diesel tanks, and chemicals were staged in secondary containment. Drill cuttings were being collected, solidified and temporarily stored in 6 dumpsters. 28 frac tanks remain staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. I did witness a 30' x 2.5' x4" deep liquid puddle east of center pad outfall that field tested at 5.58 mS conductance. A white substance was observed in the bottom of the liquid. I collected sample 9551178 from this puddle. Liquid flowing from the center pad outfall and into the sediment basin field tested at 4.82 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-179 from this area. I collected sample 9551-180 from soil in the bottom of the basin near the north-central pad outlet; the soil field tested at 2.414 mS conductance. Water in the sediment basin field tested at 2.10 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551181 near the east sediment basin overflow weir.Water flowing past the compost filter sock below the sediment basin field tested at 1.717 mS conductance. This water flows past the site LOD. I collected sample 9551182 from this area.After the inspection, I discussed the elevated conductance and sample collection with Seneca's Carlos Martinez.Vegetation is established in recently constructed areas. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1215 hours.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/18/2025
Comments: Inspection 1 of 2:On February 18, 2025, the DEP conducted a two part Incident Inspection of the Herminie Well Site (ESCGP-3 issued: 12/12/2024, expires: 12/11/2028), located in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 2/14/2025 by CNX representative Mr. Andrew. The spill report states that as CNX dug into the well pad to install secondary containment and production equipment, water and diesel fuel filled the hole. Refer to Part 2 of this inspection for details on soil samples that were collected at the time of this inspection.At the time of this inspection, the Herminie Well Site has reportedly been acquired from Apex Energy by CNX.At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 sign was at the access road entrance and inside the onsite mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, all of which had Apex Energy's name and information on it. The access road which was graveled appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. Once on the well pad, the DEP was accompanied by CNX representatives, Mr. Andrew, Chad Eisenman, and Carrie Crumpton. Mr. Andrew informed the DEP that at the time of this inspection, operations were in the drill out phase, fracking was completed last week and flowback would be starting next week. Mr. Andrew showed the DEP the spot where the first hole was dug, the DEP observed a partially frozen red substance mixed with what appeared to be frozen water that was giving off a strong petroleum based odor. Mr. Andrew stated that several test holes were then dug until CNX found a point in each direction where the fluid was no longer observed, this determined the extent of the impacted area, which appeared to approximately 60ft x 90ft with 8 total holes marked with cones to identify them as contaminated.At the time of this inspection, Penn E and R was on site with plans to excavate the area and place all contaminated material into a roll off dumpster on site. CNX could not provide the DEP with an approximated quantity of this release, but theorized that it may be over 42 gallons and plans to follow Act 2 protocol for this release. Once contaminated material is excavated, CNX hopes to have a more definitive quantity for the release. At the time of this inspection, the DEP inquired whether CNX believed any waters of the Commonwealth were impacted and Mr. Eisenman explained that the pad has catch drains all around the perimeter which discharge into an infiltration basin on the back right corner of the well site. Mr. Eisenman also stated that all catch drains and discharge points are routinely plugged during all Alteration Operations and that they were closed prior to CNX discovering the substance in these holes. The DEP also inquired when CNX hypothesizes the spill occurred, Mr. Andrew and Mr. Eisenman both stated that they believe the spill occurred when Apex Energy was operating the well pad (According to Department records, Apex Energy has not reported a spill at the Herminie well site regarding diesel fluid in this area of the well pad).Due to the spill reportedly occurring prior to CNX acquiring this well site, at the time of this inspection, the DEP collected soil samples to determine what the substance may be and to determine if this substance reached the infiltration basin prior to the drains being plugged. Refer to Part 2 for details on the collected soil samples.CNX is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations, and how CNX quantified the amount spilled.CNX will need to follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and CNX is requested to assess the impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the release.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for a release on the well pad.

A water reading of 1807 uS/cm (Photos 5-7).The soil under the valve of tank 3 was displaying non-elevated readings ranging from 856-1433 uS/cm and a water reading of 358 uS/cm (Photos 8-11).I recommend that the container with the hose is removed to avoid any fluids from reaching the ground (Photo 12).Due to the elevated conductivity noted under the valve of tank 2, the violations issued on 12/21/23 remain outstanding. No additional violations are being issued at this time.

Dump truck and mini excavator used bridge to access well. Mr. Cochran stated that a second layer of boards will be put down and side rails attached to complete the bridge deck. Gravel to be put on the either side of the bridge.Remaining violations to be lifted when clean-up is completed and bridge repair completed.

Inspection Date: 2019-12-09
Comments: The DEP conducted a follow-up inspection of Repsol's Monro G 03-142 well site located in Columbia Twp, Bradford County on 12/9/2019 at 0940 hours. The weather was 39 degrees with cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted to follow up on site conditions in relation to the violations cited on 4/25/2019. John Ciccone, WQS Trainee, was onsite with me for the inspection. We inspected the entire site for flowback activities. Some wells still have separators attached to them. PCSM BMPs are present onsite and appear to be functioning as designed. No issues with containments were found today. The majority of the site was snow and ice covered. On 4/25/2019, the DEP cited violations for a release of frac fluid and sand after an iron washout created a powerful jet stream of fluids which tore through containments. The total volume of the release was estimated to be 15 gallons. A drop-pipe was installed into the area of the release to continue to collect impacted water from the ground. Onsite today, the DEP observed this drop-pipe (see photo#4). No fluids could be field measured today. Due to the drop-pipe remaining, it is believed that follow-up sampling has not been conducted by the operator yet. Due to the clean-up of the release not being confirmed and the drop-pipe remaining, the violations noted on 4/25/2019 will remain open and are cited as outstanding. We departed the site at 1030 hours.

Brody Webster of Cabot self-reported the release to the Department on 6/24/2013 at 15:01. The Marcellus Incident report indicates the spill occurred at 8AM as a result of an overflow of a mix tank.
